sentences.text: Shri Shiva Parashar, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri Pratip Visoriya, learned Government Advocate, for respondents No.1 and 2/State.
Shri S.S. Gautam, learned counsel for respondent No.3.
Shri Harish Dixit, learned counsel for respondent No.4.
Shri N.K. Gupta, learned Senior Counsel with Shri Kamal Jain and Shri Anvesh Jain, learned counsel for respondent No.5.
This Public Interest Litigation is for a direction that respondent No.5 be directed to remove his warehouse constructed in the residential area.

It is urged that respondent No.5 has caused pollution in the entire area around the warehouse, as it empties the cold-drink bottles stored in the ware on their expiry which adds to pollution and result in erosion of soil around the said place which adversely effects the crop.
It is further contended that respondent No.5 has not constructed the pucca road connecting the warehouse to the main road, as a result whereof the vehicular movement leads to air pollution.
Respondent No.5 has filed the return, it is stated that godown has been constructed after obtaining the permission from the Gram Panchayat, Malanpur on 16.12.2009.
Whereby, the proposed map submitted for construction of warehouse has been sanctioned.

Respondent in pursuance to order dated 30.01.2019 has brought on THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH WP.4350.2016 [Dinesh Singh Yadav Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh & Ors] record the copy of blue print, receipt of building construction fee and the permission letter dated 16.12.2009 along with IA.1182/2019.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is further contended that respondent is not engaged in any kind of production of packaged soft drinks,
but has the distributorship of Coca-cola and has licence of the distributor issued by the Food and Drugs Administration under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
It is further contended that it is also registered under the Madhya Pradesh Shops & Establishment Act, 1958.
It is further contended that the place in question is utilized for commercial purpose after due permission.
And property tax for non-residential purpose is being paid.
It is urged that respondent is not the cause for any pollution as alleged.
It is contended that the pollution is because of the village in question which is situated at State Highway; whereon, the vehicular movement has resulted in causing pollution.
There is no denial of fact that the warehouse is constructed after due permission and that respondent No.5 holds the licence for distribution under the Act of 2006.

It is also not denied that Dinesh Singh Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr on 13 March, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11808161/
1 respondent No.5 is registered under 1958 Act.

sentences.text: In view whereof, we do not perceive any element of public interest being the cause in present writ petition.
The petition, being devoid of merit, is dismissed.
No costs.

(Sanjay Yadav) (Vivek Agarwal)
 Judge Judge PAWAN DHARKAR 2019.03.15 18:44:02 -07'00'
